rules: Prior context is for disambiguation only.
Do not use prior context as evidence for new L1 candidates.
Every new L1 candidate must cite only the current transcript or current idea units.

items.content: An ablation study is planned to justify combining short-term and long-term memory, which will compare a baseline (RAG only), short-term only, long-term only, and the full system.

An evaluation of the proposed "dynamic chunking" method should be conducted by comparing it against fixed-chunk and turn-by-turn baselines. The evaluation will analyze trade-offs using metrics such as the number of LLM requests (cost), output quality, and formal precision/recall against a human-annotated set of important idea units.

The team agreed to conduct an experiment comparing a dynamic transcript chunking method against two baselines: a fixed-size chunking method (e.g., 3 or 5 turns) and an iterative, per-turn summary method.

Experiments on transcript processing trade-offs (fixed-cut vs. iterative merge) will be postponed until after May 12th due to a report deadline. For now, the team will proceed by assuming the current implementation is effective without formal proof.

The memory system's forgetting mechanism is designed so that memory retrieval is based on current relevancy during an interaction, and importance is updated post-interaction. An old topic, if revisited, will have its importance boosted. Memories with a high enough importance score will never fade out.

An ablation study is planned to validate the memory system's architecture. The study will compare four configurations: a RAG-only baseline, a short-term memory only system, a long-term memory only system, and the full system. In all test cases, the working memory component will remain active to simulate an ongoing conversation.

Implement a manager-agent architecture where a central manager delegates tasks to specialized, swappable agents. An initial agent to develop is one that determines if a text segment is a complete idea unit, needs splitting, or is incomplete.

The system's data handling approach differs from a standard RAG baseline by first structuring the transcript into 'idea units'. On top of these units, the system generates higher-level conclusions for broader context and incorporates a detailed short-term memory component to track recent conversational activities.

The current dataset of 180 minutes from 5 meetings is considered potentially insufficient and of poor quality for LLM experiments, raising the need to define data sufficiency in standard terms (like tokens) and explore augmentation strategies.

To handle the evolution of information, the long-term memory system incorporates timelines. During retrieval, this allows an LLM to see when points were made, identify if they were later overturned, and determine which version is current.

To demonstrate the value of the structured memory approach, an evaluation should be conducted comparing the overall system's performance (using its structured STM/LTM) against a standard RAG system that ingests the entire raw transcript.
In the planned ablation study, the working memory component will be a constant, always active across all tested configurations to simulate an ongoing conversation.
